newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Commodity Price Index falls in November - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ Commodity Price Index falls in November - ANZ.

text.p: The average New Zealand dollar price of the country's commodity exports fell one percent in November 1996 following a 0.8 percent rise in October, ANZ Banking Group (New Zealand) Ltd said on Monday.
The corresponding average world price of New Zealand's commodity exports fell by 0.5 percent in November, compared with a 1.4 percent rise in October.

The New Zealand dollar index fell to 99.1 in November from 100.1 in August, down 11.9 percent on an annual basis, while the world price index fell to 123.6 from 124.2 over the same period, down 3.7 percent annually.
ANZ said continued weakness in world prices for wool, beef, woodpulp, logs and butter, and a drop in skin prices, contributed to the fall in the New Zealand dollar index during November.
A strong rise in the currency over the month, especially against the US dollar, also cut prices in NZ dollar terms.
The bank said a pick up in world economic growth over 1997 should lead to an increase in housing starts and consumer demand, and help underpin a gradual recovery in wool prices.
